Visible CPU count and allowed affinity can differ inside containers; record both.

usage.summary: Decode x86 CPUID leaves using the separately packaged cpuid utility.
activation: Use the resolved absolute command paths shown here. No system-wide PATH or alternatives changes are made.
notes: This is the cpuid utility, not the libcpuid library/cpuid_tool package.
CPUID reflects the virtual CPU when a hypervisor filters or emulates leaves; it is not a PMU access check.

usage.summary: Pinned Intel CPU event definitions for local event lookup and pmu-tools cache preparation.

locations.label: CPU model map
locations.purpose: Map CPU model/stepping identifiers to event JSON files

locations.label: Event tables
locations.purpose: Complete pinned upstream event and metric definitions

activation: Use the resolved absolute command paths shown here. No system-wide PATH or alternatives changes are made.

examples.description: Inspect one documented CPU event table

notes: The functional check verifies every mapfile-referenced table and parses its JSON. The hardware check separately reports whether the visible CPU has a map entry.
An AMD CPU produces a blocked Intel-map capability result; this does not mean that the Intel data package failed to install.
CPU model match is not counter qualification. Match stepping and hybrid PMU type before collecting events.
The existing seed-pmu-cache tool can prepare pmu-tools lookup from these local tables without a runtime download.

usage.summary: Use the kernel-facing perf collector with explicit event, permission and CPU capability checks.

locations.label: perf launcher
locations.purpose: APT launcher; may resolve to a kernel-specific executable

locations.label: Kernel tool installations
locations.purpose: Kernel-version-specific tool directories when supplied by APT

activation: Use the resolved absolute command paths shown here. No system-wide PATH or alternatives changes are made.
notes: A version or event-list check does not prove counter access. The optional hardware check requires positive cycles and instructions from one bounded child workload.
Known permission/device/unsupported-PMU outcomes return 77 and remain blocked, never passed. Unexpected errors or malformed/nonpositive counts fail.
The package never changes perf_event_paranoid, grants capabilities, loads modules or enables privileged containers.
CAP_PERFMON, the host kernel, PMU virtualization and the container launch profile determine available collection scopes; qualify the exact target.
